assertion_results.text: Data extraction identifies the ecosystem as RPM based on the library name (openssl-libs) and component context, not Cargo (Step 1 Ecosystem detection — read ecosystems from Ecosystem Mappings config)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md line 30: 'Ecosystem: **RPM** (system package)' with Lock File 'rpms.lock.yaml' and Category 'System package -- 1 remediation task per stream (Konflux release repo fix only)'. The ecosystem is correctly identified as RPM, not Cargo. The detection is based on the library name openssl-libs being a system package.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table includes ALL versions from the 2.2.x stream supportability matrix (2.2.0 through 2.2.4) and uses rpms.lock.yaml data for version extraction (Step 2.3)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md contains a table with all five 2.2.x versions: 2.2.0 (3.0.7-25.el9_3), 2.2.1 (3.0.7-27.el9_4), 2.2.2 (3.0.7-27.el9_4), 2.2.3 (3.0.7-28.el9_4), 2.2.4 (3.0.7-28.el9_4). Data source stated as 'git show <tag>:rpms.lock.yaml | grep openssl-libs for each pinned tag in the 2.2.x supportability matrix.' Also confirmed in affects-versions.md which shows all five versions with rpms.lock.yaml-derived openssl-libs versions.

assertion_results.text: Dependency chain context identifies openssl-libs as present in rpms.lock.yaml and uses this to determine the package origin — the lock file presence is the primary classification signal (Step 2.3.5)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md lines 32-34: 'rpms.lock.yaml: present --> explicit install' and lines 42-43: 'openssl-libs is present in rpms.lock.yaml for the 2.2.x stream, classifying it as an explicit install. The package is directly specified in the lock file, not inherited from a base image.' The lock file presence is explicitly stated as the primary classification signal (line 47: 'The rpms.lock.yaml classification (explicit install) is used as the sole determination of package origin').

assertion_results.text: Remediation creates a single task for the Konflux release repo — not the two-task upstream backport + downstream propagation flow used for source dependency ecosystems (Step 8 Remediation Task Creation — system package path)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md lines 5-6: 'Ecosystem is RPM (system package) so **1 remediation task** is created for the stream.' Only one jira.create_issue call is shown (lines 86-93) targeting the Konflux release repo rhtpa-release.0.4.z (line 29). No upstream backport task or downstream propagation task is created.

assertion_results.text: Remediation task description follows task-description-template.md format with Repository, Target Branch, Description, Implementation Notes, and Acceptance Criteria sections — Files to Modify is intentionally omitted per remediation-templates.md (Step 8 Remediation Task Creation)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md contains all required sections: '## Repository' (line 29, value: rhtpa-release.0.4.z), '## Target Branch' (line 33, value: main), '## Description' (line 37), '## Implementation Notes' (line 53), '## Acceptance Criteria' (line 68 with three checkbox items). No '## Files to Modify' section exists anywhere in the task description, confirming intentional omission.

assertion_results.text: The version impact output addresses SBOM verification in the dependency chain context — either noting that verification was skipped because cosign is not available or because external tools are prohibited, or presenting the SBOM classification result (Step 2.3.5 Optional SBOM verification)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md line 35: 'SBOM verification: skipped -- cosign not available' and lines 46-50: 'SBOM verification status: SBOM cross-validation was not performed because cosign is not available in this environment. The rpms.lock.yaml classification (explicit install) is used as the sole determination of package origin. When cosign becomes available, SBOM comparison between the final container image and the base image can confirm whether openssl-libs is added by the lock file or inherited from the FROM image.'
